clinician.trajectory_summary: A woman in her 30s with newly diagnosed type 2 diabetes mellitus presented with acute confusion, agitation, and headache. On admission, she was found to have severe DKA (glucose 628 mg/dL, pH 7.04, HCO3 8 mmol/L, anion gap 26, beta-hydroxybutyrate 2.3 mmol/L) complicated by SARS-CoV-2 infection (PCR positive, bilateral pulmonary opacities on CXR) and a hypercoagulable state (D-dimer 2264 ng/mL, fibrinogen >1000 mg/dL, thrombocytopenia 65×10⁹/L, leukocytosis 12,300×10⁹/L). Her Glasgow Coma Scale was 10 with no focal neurological deficit on initial head CT. She was intubated and sedated with ketamine, and treated with insulin infusion, sodium bicarbonate, and fluids. On ICU day 1, blood cultures returned positive for Klebsiella pneumoniae, and she was started on piperacillin-tazobactam. On ICU day 2, head CT angiography revealed worsening diffuse cerebral edema with signs of increased intracranial pressure, new duret hemorrhages of the midbrain and upper pons, non-opacification of bilateral supraclinoid internal carotid and vertebral arteries, and marked attenuation and thrombosis of the deep venous system and dural venous sinuses, confirming CVST.
